symptom_extra_hair_desc: Noticeable hair on the chin, upper lip, chest, or stomach.
symptom_acne_desc: Persistent breakouts, especially along the jawline or cheeks.
symptom_hair_thinning_desc: Noticeable thinning or widening part on the crown of your head.
symptom_weight_gain_desc: Difficulty managing weight, especially around the midsection.
symptom_dark_patches_desc: Deeper colored, velvety skin on the neck, armpits, or groin.
symptom_fertility_trouble_desc: Trying to conceive for 6 to 12 months without success.
symptom_mood_fatigue_desc: Feeling unusually fatigued, drained, or exhausted during daily routines.
symptom_mood_swings_desc: Noticeable emotional shifts, heightened irritability, or sudden tears tied to cycles.

rf_heavy_bleeding_desc: Soaking through a sanitary pad or tampon every hour for 2 or more consecutive hours.
rf_severe_pelvic_pain_desc: Sharp, intense pain in your lower belly that came on suddenly.
rf_fainting_dizziness_desc: Feeling lightheaded, dizzy, or passing out alongside bleeding.
rf_pregnancy_with_pain_desc: Could be pregnant and experiencing one-sided or sharp pelvic cramping.
rf_rapid_voice_or_hair_desc: Rapidly deepening voice or very fast hair growth in a matter of weeks.

section_associated_conditions: What These Are Commonly Associated With
pcos_awareness_title: Understanding PCOS & What Your Signs Suggest
pcos_suggestion_intro: The pattern of symptoms and cycle spacing you shared shares common features with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS).
pcos_non_diagnosis_disclaimer: Important Note: This is an awareness guide, not a medical diagnosis. Other conditions like thyroid differences, stress, or lifestyle changes can cause similar patterns. Only a qualified doctor can confirm the cause.
pcos_what_is_desc: PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) is a very common hormonal condition affecting about 1 in 5 women. It occurs when hormones fluctuate, which can lead to irregular cycles, skin or hair changes, or weight changes. It is very manageable with medical guidance and supportive daily habits.
pcos_why_see_doctor: A gynecologist can review your timeline, order simple tests (like an ultrasound or blood work), and provide gentle, personalized care.
associated_text_primary: These signs are commonly seen in conditions such as PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome), thyroid imbalances, or everyday stress and lifestyle factors.
associated_text_disclaimer: Only a qualified doctor can determine the true cause through a clinical exam and testing.
theme_cycle_desc: Variations in period timing or missing cycles for extended intervals.
theme_androgen_desc: Hormones called androgens can stimulate facial hair, persistent acne, or scalp thinning.
theme_metabolic_desc: Signs related to how the body processes sugars and energy, such as midsection weight gain or velvety skin changes.
hierarchy_section_subtitle: Hierarchical comparison of conditions doctors commonly consider. These are pattern suggestions for discussion, NEVER medical diagnoses.
hierarchy_pcos_subtitle: Very common hormonal variation affecting ovulation and metabolism
hierarchy_pcos_desc: Pattern overlap: Delayed/irregular cycles combined with androgen signs (acne, hair thinning, excess body hair) or metabolic signs (midsection weight, dark patches).
hierarchy_pcos_tests: Common doctor tests: Pelvic ultrasound (ovary follicles, endometrial lining), Free/Total Testosterone, LH/FSH ratio, Fasting Glucose.
hierarchy_pcos_questions: Doctor discussion: 'Could my combination of cycle spacing and physical signs indicate PCOS?'
hierarchy_thyroid_subtitle: Underactive thyroid gland slowing metabolism and disrupting ovulation
hierarchy_thyroid_desc: Pattern overlap: Long cycle gaps, unusual tiredness/fatigue, mood changes, and unexpected weight fluctuations.
hierarchy_thyroid_tests: Common doctor tests: Serum TSH, Free T3/T4, anti-TPO antibodies.
hierarchy_thyroid_questions: Doctor discussion: 'Would you recommend checking my TSH levels to rule out thyroid involvement?'
hierarchy_perimenopause_subtitle: Natural biological transition where ovarian hormone production gradually shifts
hierarchy_perimenopause_desc: Pattern overlap: Unpredictable cycle spacing, mood swings, night warmth or sleep changes, commonly beginning in late 30s to 40s.
hierarchy_perimenopause_tests: Common doctor tests: Serum FSH, Estradiol (E2), pelvic ultrasound.
hierarchy_perimenopause_questions: Doctor discussion: 'Could my changing cycle spacing and mood shifts be related to perimenopause?'
hierarchy_prolactin_subtitle: Pituitary hormone elevation causing missed cycles or infrequent periods
hierarchy_prolactin_desc: Pattern overlap: Months-long gaps between periods, occasional breast tenderness or headaches.
hierarchy_prolactin_tests: Common doctor tests: Serum prolactin (fasting morning sample).
hierarchy_prolactin_questions: Doctor discussion: 'Could an elevated prolactin level be causing these long cycle gaps?'
hierarchy_insulin_subtitle: Altered cellular glucose uptake frequently co-occurring with PCOS
hierarchy_insulin_desc: Pattern overlap: Midsection weight gain, acanthosis nigricans (velvety dark neck patches), sugar cravings.
hierarchy_insulin_tests: Common doctor tests: Fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, fasting insulin, lipid profile.
hierarchy_insulin_questions: Doctor discussion: 'Should we test my fasting insulin or glucose processing?'
hierarchy_fha_subtitle: Temporary suppression of reproductive signals due to stress or energy deficit
hierarchy_fha_desc: Pattern overlap: Skipped periods during high stress or illness without signs of excess androgen hormones.
hierarchy_fha_tests: Common doctor tests: Low LH/FSH, normal androgens, pelvic ultrasound.
hierarchy_fha_questions: Doctor discussion: 'Could recent lifestyle stress or dietary changes be pausing my cycle?'
doctor_gynecologist_or_urgent: Gynecologist or Immediate Urgent Care Clinic
routing_reason_primary: A gynecologist is the best first stop to evaluate menstrual patterns and reproductive wellness.
routing_reason_combined: Start with a gynecologist; an endocrinologist may also assist with deeper hormonal and metabolic balance.
routing_reason_urgent: Because of urgent symptoms, seek prompt medical attention at a clinic or hospital.
tests_disclaimer_note: Your doctor will decide which specific tests are right for your situation.
test_ultrasound_purpose: Checks the ovaries and uterine lining for characteristic patterns.
test_hormones_purpose: Evaluates levels of LH, FSH, testosterone, prolactin, and related hormones.
test_thyroid_purpose: Checks if thyroid hormone levels are influencing your menstrual cycles.
test_blood_sugar_purpose: Evaluates fasting glucose and HbA1c to see how your body manages sugar.
doctor_q_cause: Could my symptoms and cycle spacing be linked to a hormonal imbalance like PCOS or thyroid?
doctor_q_tests: Which tests (such as ultrasound or blood tests) do you recommend for me?
doctor_q_warning_signs: What warning signs should I watch out for that mean I should return right away?
doctor_q_lifestyle: What everyday nutrition, sleep, or activity changes can best support my body?
doctor_q_followup: When should we schedule a follow-up visit to review test results?
doctor_q_fertility: How might these cycle patterns affect my fertility or family planning goals?
doctor_q_cycle_regulation: What safe options exist to help make my periods more regular?
lifestyle_tip_nutrition: Nourish with balanced meals rich in fiber, whole grains, and protein.
lifestyle_tip_movement: Enjoy gentle, consistent daily movement like a 20-minute walk or light stretching.
lifestyle_tip_sleep: Prioritize 7 to 8 hours of restorative sleep to help balance natural stress hormones.
lifestyle_tip_tracking: Keep logging your cycle dates and symptom notes to bring to your doctor visit.

guide_pcos_header: Understanding PCOS: What Every Woman Needs to Know
guide_pcos_body: PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) is not a single disease, but a spectrum of hormonal and metabolic features. In India, it is estimated that nearly 1 in 5 women experience PCOS characteristics. It is driven by two main pillars: mild androgen excess and insulin resistance. With proper lifestyle habits, stress management, and medical guidance, women with PCOS live healthy, vibrant lives.
guide_menopause_body: Menopause marks the natural transition when ovaries stop releasing eggs, officially diagnosed after 12 consecutive months without a period (typically between ages 45-55). Perimenopause is the 4 to 8 year transition period prior, where cycles fluctuate, mood shifts occur, and estrogen levels vary.
guide_overlap_body: A crucial topic rarely discussed: Women who have PCOS often continue to experience unique metabolic considerations into perimenopause and menopause. Because insulin resistance and lipid profiles can persist after periods stop, continuing balanced nutrition, cardiovascular health checks, and strength training is especially beneficial. Always discuss hormone therapy (HRT) options with a gynecologist or endocrinologist.

explore_subtitle: Why Sakhi is built differently from ordinary commercial health apps.
explore_guarantee_1_title: No Cloud, No Telemetry, No Surveillance
explore_guarantee_1_desc: Most period tracking apps monetize personal user data or upload intimate logs to remote servers. Sakhi Health Card operates 100% on your device. Your data never leaves your browser.
explore_guarantee_2_desc: We strictly avoid diagnostic pronouncements. Clinical diagnosis requires blood work, pelvic imaging, and clinical history taken by a licensed medical practitioner.
explore_guarantee_3_desc: Our deterministic logic aligns with international PCOS guidelines from the World Health Organization (WHO), ACOG, and the Endocrine Society.
explore_myth_1_q: Myth: Does PCOS mean I can never have children?
explore_myth_1_a: Fact: Absolutely not. While PCOS can cause irregular ovulation, the majority of women with PCOS conceive naturally or with standard medical guidance.
explore_myth_2_q: Myth: Do only overweight women get PCOS?
explore_myth_2_a: Fact: No. Lean PCOS affects up to 25-30% of women with PCOS, where insulin resistance or androgen excess occurs regardless of body weight.
